title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-11-19
content:
Serving runtime weekly update \u001F 2026-11-19
Owner: Asha Patel
Collaborators: Diego Martinez, Priya Nair, Ethan Chen
Team: eng-serving-runtime
Status: draft

High-level summary:
- This week focused on kernel-level optimizations for attention kernels, KV-cache correctness fixes for multi-tenant workloads, and updated batching heuristics to reduce tail latency on heavy short-sequence traffic.
- We observed a 6-9% p50 p99 improvement on our medium-sized Llama derivatives in our staging perf runs after kernel tweaks. KV-cache fixes prevented a small but reproducible corruption case when reusing cached prefixes across session restores (see linked JIRA).

Highlights / wins:
- Kernel PR merged: PR #437 landed with a micro-optimizing change to the fused attention path (reduced mem copies for keys/values when use_static_kv=true). Measured ~7% lower CPU on CPU+GPU host for small-batch scenarios.
- KV cache bugfix: JIRA-INF-2981 resolved. Fix handles TTL edge case when session metadata is missing; added unit + integration tests. No customer-facing incidents observed in canary.
- Batching heuristic tweak: switched default short-seq threshold to 32 tokens and added dynamic backoff for spikes; initial canary shows 4% lower token cost for interactive workloads without increasing average latency.

Kernel work (details):
- Diego finished the fused attention refactor and added a fast path for 1-2 head-sizes in our micro-bench harness. Follow-ups: extend to int8 quantized paths (blocked on quantization API finalization).
- Metrics: staging microbench (N=1000 sequences) shows p50 -6%, p95 -5%, p99 -3% improvements on MPT-like models. Need broader matrix across seq lengths >1024.
- Next steps: land additional tests for grouped-gemm correctness across CUDA 12/13; add perf regression guard in CI for fused-attn changes.

KV cache (details):
- Root cause for corruption was missing session metadata on cached prefix invalidation when a session was recreated quickly after termination. Fixed by adding atomic write of session metadata and a lightweight session-version check before cache rebind.
- Tests: added two integration tests that simulate rapid reconnects and session restores with mixed model-variants.
- Observability: added a new cache-mismatch metric exposed in the console and an alert rule (warning at >0.1% mismatch rate over 10m).
- Action: schedule a short incident runbook review with SRE to validate rollback / cache-flush playbooks.

Batching & scheduler updates:
- Heuristics: changed short-sequence threshold from 16->32 tokens to reduce forced batching for interactive bursts.
- Adaptive backoff: implemented exponential backoff when queue depth spikes above 2x baseline to avoid blowing through token budgets.
- Bench results: in the interactive canary, saw ~3.8% lower average tokens/second cost and a small increase in p50 latency (~8ms) which is within SLA for the tier. p99 tail is unchanged.
- Follow-ups: tune the backoff factor per model family; expose a per-model override in the config with sensible defaults.

Risks & unknowns:
- Quantized kernel path parity: some fused-attn micro-optimizations are not yet validated for int8/int4. Could cause minor accuracy differences - research team flagged this as medium risk.
- Long-sequence perf: improvements concentrated on short->medium sequences; we need a separate matrix for >2k tokens workloads.
- Canary coverage: the current canary does not exercise multi-tenant eviction patterns that surface under Dedicated load. Need to expand.

Blockers:
- CUDA 13 infra on some CI runners is flaky; blocks completing grouped-gemm compatibility tests. Working with infra to repro and stabilize.
- Quantization API finalization (research) - blocks int8 verification for new kernel paths.

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2026-11-19):
Attendees: Asha, Diego, Priya, Ethan, Sam (SRE)
- Diego: kernel PR landed; will follow up on quantized paths.
- Priya: KV-cache fix in; added metrics & alerting. Ask SRE to validate runbook.
- Ethan: batching heuristic adjustment rolled to canary; monitoring cost and latency.
- Sam (SRE): will run chaos test for rapid reconnects next Tue and validate cache-flush plays.
- Action owners assigned (see action items).

Action items (owner - due):
- Add grouped-gemm tests across CUDA 12/13 to CI (Diego - 2026-11-26).
- Run chaos reconnect test and report results (Sam - 2026-11-24).
- Add per-model batching override and doc in console (Ethan + Docs - 2026-11-30).
- Review incident runbook for KV-cache flush (Priya + SRE - 2026-11-23).
- Start int8 verification plan with Research (Asha - 2026-12-03).

Notes / context / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/437
- Jira: JIRA-INF-2981 (KV cache corruption)
- Confluence: Serving Runtime Kernel Design (draft)

Next week goals:
- Stabilize CI for grouped-gemm; land CI guard rails.
- Complete chaos test for KV-cache and validate alarms.
- Extend perf matrix to include long-sequence (>2048) runs.
- Begin int8 verification experiments on a small model family in staging.

Short personal notes / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Follow up with infra on CUDA runner parity - get ETA.
- Draft quick guide for on-call about cache-mismatch alert.
- Book 30m with Research to scope int8 testing plan.

End of update.
